newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk military chief leaves for Israel visit.
newsitem.headline: Turk military chief leaves for Israel visit.

text.p: Turkey's armed forces chief General Ismail Hakki Karadayi left on Monday for a three-day visit to Israel in a further sign of strengthening military cooperation between the two countries.
"He left this morning for a planned official visit to Israel," the official told Reuters. He said the visit would last until Thursday, but gave no more details.

Moslem but secular Turkey and Israel have signed two military accords, which involve allowing Israeli jets on training flights in Turkish airspace and upgrading of the Turkish Air Force's fleet of F-4 Phantom jets by Israel.

The accords were condemned by Iran and many in the Arab world. Ankara's closer links with Israel also drew strong protests at the time from Islamists in Turkey. Since becoming prime minister eight months ago Islamist Welfare Party leader Necmettin Erbakan has toned down his once fervent criticism.
However, a Welfare mayor was detained by police earlier this month after organising an anti-Israel protest near the capital.
